Condensing Water System Sequences
Sequence – Condenser Water System – Chiller Plant:
System Off – When the system is off:
The chillers shall be off
The pumps shall be off.
The fans shall be off.
The tower bypass valves shall be closed.
The tower isolation valves shall be closed.
System Start-up – System start-up shall be initiated:
Automatically by the EMCS, when the chiller plant is enabled.
System Operation – When system start-up has been initiated:
The towers and pumps shall be lead/lag and rotated weekly at a time and on a day of the week when the chiller
plant is not in operation. Rotation shall be based on accumulated runtime for each type of equipment. When the
condenser water system is activated, the EMCS shall open all tower isolation valve on the lead tower. When the
valve end switch has been proven open, the EMCS shall enable the pump associated with the lead chiller. A
current switch shall prove the pump status at the EMCS, which shall generate an alarm, if the switch is not made
within 45 seconds (adj.). There shall also be a 10 second (adj.) de-bounce time to prevent nuisance alarm from a
bouncing switchIf. the pump run status is not proven, the EMCS shall discontinue the enable signal to the pump
and rotate pumps and chillers.
There should be one tower more on than chiller quantity. For example, if there is one chiller on, there should be
two cooling cells active. If there are two chillers on, there should be three cooling tower cells active.
When the lead pump status is proven, the EMCS shall enable the lead chiller. A flow switch in the condenser
water piping shall complete the circuit to the chiller factory installed controller proving that flow has been
established. If the chiller alarm input closes (indicating that the chiller has alarm), the EMCS shall generate an
alarm, discontinue the enable signal to the lead chiller and shall rotate to the lag chiller. The lag chiller shall
become the lead chiller.
When one chiller is in operation, then two cooling tower cells shall be in operation. When two or three chillers
are in operation, then three cooling tower cells shall be in operation.
A temperature sensor monitoring the tower leaving water shall be used to modulate the speed of the tower fans.
A PID control loop shall modulate the speed of the fans from their minimum speed to their maximum speed as
the temperature deviates from set point. All active tower fans shall be modulated with the same ramp signal. If
the tower fan is operating at its minimum speed and the leaving water temperature is below set point, than the
fan shall be de-energized.
The tower leaving water temperature sensor shall be used to modulate the tower bypass valves. A PID control
loop shall modulate bypass valve open to maintain set point.
When a chiller is to be disabled, the EMCS shall discontinue the command for the chiller to run. The EMCS shall
continue to hold open the isolation valves until the chiller status has indicated that it is off. The EMCS shall close
the valve.
The EMCS shall monitor the outside air temperature and humidity. The EMCS shall calculate the outside air
enthalpy, wet bulb temperature and dew point temperature. These valves shall be displayed on all air and water
system graphics.
When the outdoor air temperature id below 34°F (adj.), the pumps shall run at a minimum speed to prevent
freezing.
System Set points – The set points for the system shall be set as follows:
The tower leaving water temperature set point shall be 65°F (adj.).
